basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 14.' and it opens '(Cap. XIX.—Vers. 14.) Et locutus est ad generos suos, qui acceperant filias ejus. Quia'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XIX.—Vers. 14.) Et locutus est ad generos suos, qui acceperant filias ejus. Quia postea duae filiae Lot virgines fuisse dicuntur (de quibus et ipse dudum ad Sodomaeos dixerat: Ecce duae filiae meae, quae non cognoverunt virum), et nunc Scriptura commemorat eum habuisse generos; nonnulli arbitrantur illas, quae viros habuerunt, in Sodomis remansisse, et eas exisse cum patre, quae virgines fuerunt. Quod cum Scriptura non dicat, Hebraea veritas exponenda est, in qua scribitur: Egressus est Lot, et locutus est ad sponsos, qui accepturi erant filias ejus. Necdum igitur virgines filiae matrimonio fuerant copulatae.
